content.comment_body: Hello, I'm transferring values from an HMI to [product_name] using Network Analog Input (NAI). My goal is to retain the last value on the PLC, even when the HMI or both devices are powered off. On other PLC models, there's a dedicated I/O for this purpose, but how can this be done in [product_name]? Is there a special memory or method to save the last transmitted value?
Hello [user_name], [product_name] has a retentive memory area. You might be able to save the necessary data as retentive so it is not lost after a power cycle. Memory space and circuit program size

The challenge lies in the VM memory area, as it is not retentive. If instead of reading values via NAI, you input them directly into the parameters of mathematical instructions, these values are saved to the flash memory of [product_name]. You can achieve this through Parameter-VM-Mapping.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring ways to persist I/O values on [product_name] PLC after rebooting, highlighting the absence of an obvious retentive memory fit for this purpose. There is uncertainty about the persistency of the VM memory area, with users investigating alternatives to keep data after power loss. Workarounds include mapping values to parameters stored in device flash memory, bypassing default network input or volatile memory areas.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to provide a straightforward way, such as a specific memory configuration or built-in feature, to retain the last I/O value even after a power loss or restart.
